symptom: `ALTER WORKFLOW ... REPLACE ACTIVITY userTask1 WITH <identical user task>` reported 'Altered workflow' and reset the task's on-created microflow (Workflows$MicroflowBasedEvent -> NoEvent). A `create or modify` of a workflow with an on-created microflow, workflow event handlers, a non-default multi-user completion rule or an AI agent task would lose them the same way: check, exec and mx check all clean.
cause: Both writers rebuild a workflow activity from the AST and write a default for every property MDL has no spelling for: OnCreatedEvent = NoEvent, CompletionCriteria = Consensus on the first outcome, OnWorkflowEvent = empty list; describe prints an AIAgentTaskActivity as a `-- [Workflows$...]` comment. checkNoDroppedWorkflowConstructs guarded only event sub-processes and boundary events.
fix: checkNoDroppedWorkflowConstructs collects every inexpressible construct from the raw unit (studioProOnlyWorkflowState / rawActivityState) and refuses the rewrite listing them all; validateAlterReplaceKeepsStudioProState refuses REPLACE ACTIVITY on an activity whose raw document holds one (matched by Name, unique per CE0495). Consensus falling back to the first outcome is not refused — it is what the rebuild writes and what the reference stores.
insight: Guard-don't-drop needs a Studio Pro reference to be anything but a guess: until one existed the risk was code-derived, and the reference both confirmed the loss (REPLACE, measured) and set the exact threshold — its Consensus fallback points at the FIRST outcome, which is what mxcli writes, so refusing every Consensus would have refused every multi-user rewrite. Measure the control on the same document: SET ACTIVITY kept the microflow, which is what proves REPLACE's rebuild is the cause rather than ALTER as a whole. A raw-unit walk of `$Type` strings is also how to guard constructs the semantic model does not carry at all (completion criteria, workflow event handlers).
